title: Choose a level of accuracy that fits the limits of measurement

sections.skill: Choose a level of accuracy that fits the limits of measurement

questions.skill: Choose a level of accuracy that fits the limits of measurement
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A ruler measures to the nearest 0.1 cm. A rectangle measures 4.3 cm by 2.7 cm, and a calculator gives its area as 11.61 square cm. Which report of the area best fits the accuracy of the measurements?
questions.prompt_markup:
A ruler measures to the nearest 0.1 cm. A rectangle measures 4.3 cm by 2.7 cm, and a calculator gives its area as 11.61 square cm.
Which report of the area best fits the accuracy of the measurements?
questions.grading_note: Each length could be off by 0.05 cm, so the true area is between about 11.3 and 12.0 square cm; the hundredths digit is not known.

questions.skill: Choose a level of accuracy that fits the limits of measurement
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A stopwatch reads to the nearest 0.1 second. A runner covers 100 m in 12.4 seconds, and a calculator gives 8.0645161 meters per second. Report the speed to a sensible accuracy.
questions.prompt_markup:
A stopwatch reads to the nearest 0.1 second. A runner covers 100 m in 12.4 seconds, and a calculator gives 8.0645161 meters per second.
Report the speed to a sensible accuracy.
questions.grading_note: Form required: a rounded value. 8.1 or 8.06 m/s is accepted; the true speed is between about 8.03 and 8.10 m/s, so more digits are not meaningful.

questions.grading_note: The tape measures to the nearest centimeter, so report whole centimeters.

questions.correct_answer: No. 40 ÷ 5 = 8, so the answer should be about 8.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation.

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A cylinder has a radius of 3.0 cm and a height of 10.0 cm. Find its volume to the nearest cubic centimeter.
questions.prompt_markup:
A cylinder has a radius of 3.0 cm and a height of 10.0 cm.
Find its volume to the nearest cubic centimeter.
questions.grading_note: Form required: rounded to the nearest whole number. V = π · 3² · 10 = 90π ≈ 282.7.

sections.skill: Use the margin of error of a sample survey
sections.nearest_connection: The accuracy a measurement supports leads to the accuracy of an estimate from a sample, given by its margin of error.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use the margin of error of a sample survey
questions.nearest_connection: The accuracy a measurement supports leads to the accuracy of an estimate from a sample, given by its margin of error.
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A poll reports that 54% of voters support a plan, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. What interval of values for the true percent does this give?
questions.prompt_markup:
A poll reports that 54% of voters support a plan, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points.
What interval of values for the true percent does this give?
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent form. 54% - 3% to 54% + 3%.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Use the margin of error of a sample survey
questions.nearest_connection: The accuracy a measurement supports leads to the accuracy of an estimate from a sample, given by its margin of error.
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A poll reports 54% support with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. Do the results suggest that a majority supports the plan? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
A poll reports 54% support with a margin of error of 3 percentage points.
Do the results suggest that a majority supports the plan? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. Every value in the interval, 51% to 57%, is above 50%.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation that uses the interval.
